title.value: Efficient Diversity-Preserving Diffusion Alignment via Gradient-Informed GFlowNets
title.justification: The title refers to a key contribution of the paper which is the introduction of a new method for finetuning diffusion models, called Nabla-GFlowNet, that is efficient in preserving diversity and alignment through gradient-informed techniques.
title.quote: We propose ∇-DB and the pretrained-model-aware variant residual ∇-DB, the objectives that efficiently leverage the rich information in reward gradients in a principled and probabilistic way.

analysis.description: This paper introduces Nabla-GFlowNet, a reinforcement learning method for finetuning large diffusion models, leveraging reward gradients to achieve efficient diversity-preserving alignment. The method is shown to be effective in finetuning Stable Diffusion models while preserving diversity and prior knowledge using a novel gradient-informed approach.

type.justification: The study provides experimental results showcasing the effectiveness of the Nabla-GFlowNet method on real-world tasks, validating the approach through empirical evidence.
type.quote: We empirically show that with the proposed residual ∇-DB objective, we may achieve diversity- and prior-preserving yet fast finetuning and alignment of diffusion models.

name.justification: The primary research field is Reinforcement Learning as the paper proposes a novel reinforcement learning objective and method, Nabla-GFlowNet, for finetuning diffusion models based on reward gradients.
name.quote: Our ∇-GFlowNet is the first GFlowNet method that considers first-order information in reward signals, and is closely connected to soft reinforcement learning.

name.justification: The paper focuses on improving generative models, specifically diffusion models, by enhancing their alignment through a novel method that preserves sample diversity.
name.quote: Diffusion models are a powerful class of generative models that model highly complex data distributions with sequential denoising steps.

name.justification: The paper demonstrates the method on tasks within the domain of image synthesis, a key area in computer vision.
name.quote: We show that our proposed method achieves fast yet diversity- and prior-preserving finetuning of Stable Diffusion, a large-scale text-conditioned image diffusion model.

name.justification: Stable Diffusion is a large-scale text-conditioned image diffusion model that the paper aims to finetune using Nabla-GFlowNet.
name.quote: We show that our proposed method achieves fast yet diversity- and prior-preserving finetuning of Stable Diffusion, a large-scale text-conditioned image diffusion model.

is_contributed.justification: Stable Diffusion itself is not contributed by this paper but used as a testbed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the new finetuning method.
is_contributed.quote: We show that our proposed method achieves fast yet diversity- and prior-preserving finetuning of Stable Diffusion, a large-scale text-conditioned image diffusion model.

is_executed.justification: The paper involves empirical tests where Stable Diffusion models are executed to evaluate the finetuning methods.
is_executed.quote: We empirically show that with the proposed residual ∇-DB objective, we may achieve diversity- and prior-preserving yet fast finetuning and alignment of diffusion models.

is_compared.justification: The performance of the finetuning method on Stable Diffusion is compared against other models and methods, as mentioned in the experimental results.
is_compared.quote: Our proposed residual ∇-DB is able to achieve comparable convergence speed, measured in update steps, to that of the gradient-free baselines while those diversity-aware baselines fail to do so.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The referenced paper title for Stable Diffusion is 'High-resolution image synthesis with latent diffusion models'.
referenced_paper_title.quote: StableDiffusion-v1.5 [51] is used as the base model.

name.justification: The LAION-aesthetic dataset, which includes large-scale human preference data, is utilized to train some of the reward functions used in the paper.
name.quote: For the main experiments, we consider two reward functions: Aesthetic Score [28], Human Preference Score (HPSv2) [69, 70] and ImageReward [71], all of which trained on large-scale human preference datasets such as LAION-aesthetic [28] and predict the logarithm of reward values.
